analytic.title: Integrated Energy Monitoring and Control System with Tri-Node ESP32 Architecture

div.p: Efficient energy management requires real-time monitoring and control. This study proposes an IoT-based energy monitoring and control system using a tri-node ESP32 architecture with a Transmitter, Receiver, and Remote module. The system utilizes a PZEM-004T sensor to measure voltage, current, power, energy, frequency, and power factor, transmitting real-time data to an OLED display. The Remote module controls a relay for load switching. Performance evaluation shows high measurement accuracy with a maximum power deviation of 5.46%. The system maintains a 1012.8 ms data latency and 581 ms relay switching delay, ensuring fast response. Network testing confirms reliable operation under strong and moderate Wi-Fi, though latency increases to 1776.49 ms in weak signal conditions. The system effectively integrates real-time monitoring, responsive control, and stable communication, making it suitable for IoT-based energy management applications.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Efficient energy management is a critical challenge in both residential and industrial sectors, driven by increasing global energy demand. The Internet of Things (IoT) technology has facilitated the development of smart monitoring systems that provide real-time data acquisition and remote access [1]. Among the various IoT platforms, ESP32 has gained popularity due to its low cost, built-in Wi-Fi connectivity, and compatibility with multiple sensors [2], [3]. However, existing energy monitoring systems predominantly focus on data collection and lack integrated real-time control mechanisms, which are crucial for optimizing energy consumption [4].

Previous studies have developed IoT-based energy monitoring systems using PZEM-004T sensors to measure electrical parameters such as voltage, current, power, energy, frequency, and power factor [5]. These studies effectively track energy consumption but often require additional manual components or separate control systems, leading to inefficiencies in remote energy regulation. Furthermore, communication latency and limited response times in existing implementations hinder real-time decision-making for energy optimization [6], [7].

To address these limitations, this study proposes an integrated energy monitoring and control system based on a tri-node ESP32 architecture. The system consists of a transmitter, receiver, and remote ESP32 module, enabling real-time monitoring and remote control through a relay-based mechanism. The transmitter collects live energy data using the PZEM-004T sensor and transmits it wirelessly to the receiver, which displays the data on an OLED screen. Additionally, the remote ESP32 unit provides direct relay control, allowing users to regulate energy usage with minimal latency [8].

Compared to previous works, this system offers a dualfunction approach, integrating real-time monitoring and control within a single platform. It ensures low-latency communication, high measurement accuracy, and scalability for various applications, including residential, commercial, and industrial energy management. The proposed system enhances energy efficiency and sustainability, supporting global efforts to reduce carbon footprints [9], [10].

The remainder of this paper is structured as follows: Section II details the system architecture and methodology, including hardware and software implementation. Section III presents the experimental setup and performance evaluation, highlighting the system's response time and accuracy. Section IV provides a comparative discussion of the findings, and Section V concludes the study while outlining future research directions.

div.head: II. METHODOLOGY
div.p: This section describes the design and implementation of the proposed tri-node ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system, which integrates a transmitter for energy measurement, a receiver for real-time data visualization, and a remote ESP32 for relay-based energy control. The methodology covers system architecture, hardware and software implementation, and experimental evaluation, ensuring accurate energy monitoring, low-latency response, and reliable wireless communication [11]. Experimental validation is conducted to assess measurement accuracy, system responsiveness, and communication stability under different conditions.

div.head: A. System Architecture
div.p: The proposed system is designed using a tri-node ESP32 architecture, integrating a transmitter for energy data acquisition, a receiver for data visualization, and a remote ESP32 for relay-based control. This architecture ensures realtime monitoring, low-latency communication, and efficient remote switching, addressing the limitations of conventional energy monitoring systems that lack integrated control functionalities.
The system consists of three primary modules:

1. Transmitter Node: Responsible for real-time energy parameter measurement using a PZEM-004T sensor. The ESP32 reads electrical data, including voltage, current, power, energy, frequency, and power factor, and transmits it wirelessly to the receiver via Wi-Fi communication.

2. Receiver Node: Functions as the central monitoring unit, processing and displaying the received energy data on an OLED screen. This node ensures real-time visualization and provides users with easy access to energy consumption insights.

3. Remote Control Node: Enables relay-based control over electrical loads connected to the transmitter. The remote ESP32 module communicates with the transmitter using predefined HTTP commands, allowing users to turn devices ON/OFF remotely with minimal response time.

The overall system architecture, including the communication between the transmitter, receiver, and remote ESP32 modules, is illustrated in Fig. 1. For communication, the system employs Wi-Fi-based HTTP requests, where the transmitter acts as a client sending periodic GET requests to the receiver (server). Similarly, the remote ESP32 module sends HTTP control signals to the transmitter to toggle the relay state. This configuration ensures low-latency operation, allowing real-time control and monitoring.

div.head: B. Hardware Implementation
div.p: The hardware components in this study were selected based on their efficiency, low power consumption, and realtime data processing capabilities. The system consists of the following key components:
• ESP32 Development Board: The main microcontroller for all three nodes, supporting Wi-Fi communication and fast processing for real-time monitoring.
• PZEM-004T Energy Meter: Measures voltage, current, power, energy, frequency, and power factor via the UART communication protocol.
• Relay Module: Allows remote switching of electrical loads based on commands from the remote ESP32.
• OLED Display (0.96-inch SSD1306): Provides realtime energy visualization from the receiver module.
• Power Supply (5V): Ensures stable voltage to maintain reliable system performance.

div.head: C. Software Implementation
div.p: The software for this system was developed using Arduino IDE, utilizing multiple libraries for sensor data acquisition, wireless communication, and real-time data visualization. The system consists of three primary modules: Transmitter, Receiver, and Remote Control, each playing a distinct role in ensuring seamless energy monitoring and control. The Transmitter Module is responsible for reading electrical parameters such as voltage, current, power, energy, frequency, and power factor using the PZEM-004T sensor. This data is processed and made available via an HTTP server, allowing the Receiver Module to fetch the information in realtime. Additionally, the Transmitter responds to control signals from the Remote Control Module, enabling relay activation to manage electrical loads.

The Receiver Module functions as a data processing and visualization unit, continuously retrieving energy data from the Transmitter via HTTP GET requests. The received information is then displayed on an OLED screen using the U8g2 library, ensuring users have access to up-to-date energy consumption insights. To maintain system efficiency, the Receiver updates the display every 5 seconds, minimizing latency while providing real-time monitoring.

Meanwhile, the Remote Control Module allows users to control electrical loads remotely. The ESP32-based Remote Control detects push-button inputs, which trigger the transmission of HTTP relay control commands to the Transmitter Module. Upon receiving these commands, the Transmitter activates or deactivates the corresponding relay, adjusting the state of connected electrical devices. To prevent unintended relay activations, a debounce mechanism is implemented in the Remote Module, ensuring accurate and responsive control.

The software execution flowchart illustrating the complete system operation is shown in Fig. 5. The process begins with the Transmitter reading sensor data and transmitting it via HTTP to the Receiver. The Receiver then fetches and processes the data for real-time display. Simultaneously, the Remote Module monitors for user input and, when a button is pressed, sends an HTTP command to toggle the relay. The Transmitter receives this command and switches the corresponding relay accordingly, completing the control loop. This continuous cycle ensures accurate, responsive, and lowlatency energy monitoring and control.

div.head: D. Experimental Setup & Testing
div.p: The performance of the ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system was evaluated through a series of experiments focusing on energy measurement accuracy, response time, and network stability. These experiments were conducted in a controlled laboratory environment to ensure consistency and minimal interference [12].

The first experiment aimed to validate the accuracy of the PZEM-004T energy sensor by comparing its readings with a Hioki AC Clamp Power Meter, a widely recognized commercial power measurement device. Various electrical loads, including irons, heaters, air conditioners, televisions, and water pumps, were used to assess voltage, current, power, and power factor (Cos φ). The third experiment examined the stability of Wi-Fibased HTTP communication, focusing on the impact of signal strength on data transmission latency. The system was tested while connected to a Wi-Fi network with an average speed of 20 Mbps, ensuring a consistent network environment during measurements.
To evaluate network performance, the system was tested under three different signal conditions:
• Strong signal (-50 dBm, 1-2 meters from the router)
• Moderate signal (-50 dBm to -70 dBm, 3-4 meters from the router)
• Weak signal (<-70 dBm, more than 5 meters from the router or with physical obstacles)

The Wi-Fi signal strength (RSSI -Received Signal Strength Indicator) was measured using the WiFi.RSSI() function of the ESP32, while latency was recorded based on HTTP request-response timestamps to evaluate the system's ability to maintain stable and reliable data communication under different network conditions. This experiment aimed to determine how variations in signal strength impact data transmission latency, which is crucial for ensuring reliable real-time monitoring in IoT applications. The results from these experiments, including energy accuracy validation, response time analysis, and network stability assessment, are presented in Section III: Experimental Results & Analysis, providing a comprehensive overview of the system's performance.

div.head: III. EXPERIMENTAL RESULTS & ANALYSIS
div.p: To evaluate the performance of the ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system, several experiments were conducted, including energy measurement accuracy validation, response time analysis, and network stability testing. The experimental results are presented and analyzed in this section to determine the system's reliability and efficiency.

div.head: A. Energy Measurement Accuracy Analysis
div.p: The energy measurement results comparing the PZEM-004T sensor and the Hioki AC Clamp Power Meter are summarized in Table I. The table presents voltage, current, power, and power factor (Cos φ) readings for various electrical loads, along with the percentage error in power measurement.

Based on the data, the PZEM-004T demonstrates high accuracy in voltage measurement, with a maximum deviation of only 0.5% compared to the Hioki Power Meter. This indicates that the sensor reliably captures real-time voltage levels across different loads. However, current and power measurements show slightly higher deviations, particularly for high-power loads. The highest power error recorded was 5.46% for the air conditioner load, while other appliances maintained an error below 5%, confirming that the PZEM-004T is suitable for general energy monitoring applications. The power factor (Cos φ) values recorded by the PZEM-004T are also consistent with the Hioki Power Meter, with minimal variation. This suggests that the sensor can effectively monitor reactive power components, making it useful for energy efficiency analysis.

Overall, the PZEM-004T provides reliable energy measurement performance, with acceptable accuracy for realtime monitoring applications. While minor deviations exist, particularly in current and power readings, these can be attributed to sensor resolution and internal calibration factors. To enhance precision, software-based calibration techniques or compensation algorithms could be explored in future improvements.

div.head: B. Response Time Analysis
div.p: The response time of the ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system was evaluated by measuring two key latency parameters: data transmission latency and relay switching delay. The data transmission latency represents the time taken for the Transmitter module to send energy data via HTTP and for the Receiver module to display it on the OLED screen. Meanwhile, the relay switching delay measures the time elapsed from a button press on the Remote Control module to the activation of the relay on the Transmitter module.

The first test focused on data transmission latency, where the Transmitter sends energy data every 5 seconds, and the Receiver updates the OLED display accordingly. Table II presents the recorded timestamps for multiple trials. The average latency observed in the experiment is 1.013 seconds, indicating a consistent delay in updating the OLED screen after data transmission. The experimental results indicate that the average data transmission latency is approximately 1.013 seconds, suggesting that the system maintains a consistent HTTP communication delay between the Transmitter and Receiver. This delay is expected due to the network request processing time and OLED display update speed. However, since the system updates data every 5 seconds, this latency does not significantly affect real-time monitoring performance.

The second test measured relay switching delay, where the Remote Control sends a command to the Transmitter every 10 seconds to toggle the relay. Table III presents the timestamps and recorded delays for multiple trials. The average relay delay is approximately 0.58 seconds, indicating fast relay activation after a user input. The experimental data confirms that the relay switching response time is minimal, with an average delay of 0.58 seconds. This low latency ensures that relay activation occurs almost instantly after a button press, making the system highly efficient for remote control applications.

Overall, the response time analysis confirms that the ESP32-based system is highly responsive, with low latency in data transmission and fast relay switching performance. The measured delays are within acceptable limits, ensuring a smooth user experience for both real-time monitoring and remote control.

div.head: C. Network Stability Analysis
div.p: The stability of the ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system was analyzed by measuring Wi-Fi signal strength and network latency. These factors directly impact the efficiency of data transmission and system responsiveness. The results of the network stability test are presented in Table IV. The experimental results indicate that when the Wi-Fi signal strength is strong (> -50 dBm), the system maintains minimal latency (~810.24 ms), ensuring stable and real-time data transmission. As the signal strength weakens (-50 dBm to -70 dBm), latency increases to 1152.76 ms, introducing a slight delay in OLED updates. However, under weak signal conditions (< -70 dBm), latency significantly increases to 1776.49 ms (~1.78 seconds), which can cause noticeable delays in data updates and occasional interruptions in HTTP communication.

div.head: D. Summary of Findings
div.p: The experimental results confirm that the ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system performs reliably in terms of energy measurement accuracy, response time, and network stability. The PZEM-004T sensor demonstrated high accuracy, with voltage and power factor deviations of less than 0.5%, while current and power measurements had a maximum error of 5.46%, ensuring reliable real-time energy monitoring. In terms of response time, the system maintained an average data transmission latency of 1012.8 ms and a relay switching delay of 581 ms, enabling fast and efficient remote control. The network stability test showed that strong and moderate Wi-Fi conditions supported stable operation, with latencies of 810.24 ms and 1152.76 ms, respectively. However, in weak signal conditions (< -70 dBm), latency increased to 1776.49 ms (~1.78 seconds), which could cause noticeable delays in data updates. These findings highlight that the system performs well under normal conditions but may require optimizations such as MQTT/WebSockets for improved network efficiency. Overall, the tri-node ESP32 architecture successfully integrates real-time monitoring, fast response times, and stable communication, making it a reliable solution for IoT-based energy management applications.

div.head: IV. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORKS
div.p: This study successfully developed and evaluated an ESP32-based energy monitoring and control system using a tri-node architecture consisting of a Transmitter, Receiver, and Remote Control module. The system demonstrated high accuracy in energy measurement, with voltage and power factor deviations below 0.5%, while current and power readings had a maximum error of 5.46%, ensuring reliability for real-time monitoring. The response time analysis confirmed low latency, with an average data transmission delay of 1012.8 ms and a relay switching delay of 581 ms, enabling fast and efficient remote control. The network stability evaluation revealed that the system operates optimally under strong and moderate Wi-Fi conditions, but latency increases significantly to 1776.49 ms (~1.78 seconds) in weak signal environments, potentially affecting real-time performance. Future improvements may include network optimization using MQTT/WebSockets, enhanced data transmission algorithms, and hardware modifications for better relay responsiveness. Overall, the system provides a reliable IoT-based solution for energy management applications, balancing monitoring accuracy, control efficiency, and communication stability.
